cells.tense: You are imagining inside what you share with people, and the imagining and the living are one act.
cells.act: let the will and the wanting go the same way
cells.ask: Take one practice or story the group keeps, spend ten minutes with it exactly as it is now, and change nothing about it.
cells.core:
You are among people who keep a meaning alive together, and you are not straining toward a future version of it. What you imagined for this shared thing has arrived in some measure, and you are treating that as enough. The fullness is not because everything is perfect; it is because the thing has been felt. That is a quiet, available kind of plenty, and it has a place in a life that runs on shared meaning.
The next move is not to find a better thing. Take one practice or story the group keeps, spend ten minutes with it exactly as it is now, and change nothing about it. Attend to how it is rather than how it might improve. What is already full grows by being used, not by being guarded, and use is what you are being asked to give it.

cells.tense: You are pushing a shared meaning toward a future it never agreed to, and the push has become a grip.
cells.ask: Name one shared practice you have been defending, hand it to someone else for a season with no notes and no corrections, and keep your hands off it.
cells.core:
In the shared meaning you carry, the imagining has run ahead. You can see what this tradition could be, and the gap between that and what it is now has started to feel like something that has to close. So you tend it hard: you refine the wording, you correct the way it is done, you hold it tighter than it can be held. Anyone near it can feel the grip, and they have stopped bringing you the parts they would like to keep.
Growing a thing without forcing it is the move here. Name one shared practice you have been defending, hand it to someone else for a season with no notes and no corrections, and keep your hands off it. You retain the part that is yours and watch the rest. If it lives without you, you have your answer.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding the shared thing tighter than it can be held.

cells.tense: A shared meaning used to be something you could imagine, and now you describe it from outside.
cells.act: write both sides of it on one page and close the page
cells.ask: Write what the group keeps and what it has stopped keeping on one page, close the page, and set it aside for a week.
cells.core:
There was a shared thing — a practice, a story the group told about itself — and you were part of it. Then you stepped outside, and the outside has become where you live. You can describe what it was, and you can describe what it is now, and the two sit in you without meeting. What made the thing worth keeping has gone quiet, and no new imagining has started where it was.
Re-entering is not the move, and declaring it dead is not either. Write what the group keeps and what it has stopped keeping on one page, close the page, and set it aside for a week. That holding is not indecision; it is the plain ground where imagining can begin again. You do not have to know which one wins.

cells.tense: A shared meaning is being kept alive in this room, and the room does not name whose hand is on it.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Watch one thing the group says it values and one thing it does, hold both in view for a day, and reach no verdict on either.
cells.core:
You are keeping a shared meaning alive — a wording, a way the group does it, a story it tells about itself. Wherever the practice has drifted, it has drifted back toward something true because you noticed. When someone asks, you say the group just cares about getting it right. That care has your hand on it. You are steering the shared thing, and your account of it is that it steers itself.
What is left is to see the distinction you have been making without claiming it. Watch one thing the group says it values and one thing it does, hold both in view for a day, and reach no verdict on either. Separate them clearly and both stand. That is refining perception, and when you know you are doing it, the shared thing is authored on purpose.
